definition: To carefully judge the quality, importance, or value of something.
example: Students need to evaluate sources critically for their research papers.

definition: To reverse the effect of an action, making it as if it never happened.
example: I accidentally deleted the file, but I could undo the action.

definition: An angry argument or disagreement between people.
example: The neighbours had a quarrel over the loud music.

definition: A dirty mark on something that is difficult to remove.
example: He accidentally spilled coffee and left a stain on his shirt.

definition: Happening or existing in all parts of a particular country.
example: There was a nationwide strike by transport workers last week.

definition: The quality that makes something funny, or the ability to laugh and be amused.
example: He has a good sense of humour and always makes people laugh.

definition: To have something available to give or use because it is extra.
example: Do you have a spare pen I could borrow?

definition: To officially give or allow something, often money for a specific purpose.
example: The university granted him a scholarship to study abroad.

definition: Based on clear thought and reason, rather than emotions.
example: It's important to make rational decisions in a crisis.

definition: Knowledge or understanding of a situation or fact.
example: Public awareness of environmental issues has increased recently.

definition: To often do something or be in a certain way.
example: People tend to eat more in winter than in summer.

definition: A slight suggestion or piece of information that helps you understand something.
example: She dropped a hint that she wanted a new car for her birthday.

definition: Not often; rarely.
example: He seldom visits his relatives who live far away.

definition: Connected with literature or the writing of books, poems, and plays.
example: She has a strong interest in literary criticism.

definition: Showing the usual characteristics or qualities of a particular type of person or thing.
example: A typical day for me starts with a cup of coffee.

definition: In every part of a place; during the whole period of time.
example: The exhibition was popular throughout the summer.

definition: Physical injury or other damage.
example: Smoking can cause serious harm to your health.

definition: To expect something to happen and prepare for it.
example: We anticipate a lot of visitors to the festival this year.

definition: An idea, feeling, or opinion about something or someone, especially one formed without conscious thought or on the basis of little evidence.
example: Her clear presentation made a very good impression on the audience.

definition: Having the necessary tools, clothes, or other things for a particular purpose.
example: The kitchen was equipped with all modern appliances.

definition: The state of being made up of different types of people or things.
example: The city is known for its cultural diversity.

definition: The ability to change or be changed easily according to the situation.
example: Working from home offers greater flexibility for employees.

definition: The degree to which something has spread or is true.
example: It's hard to measure the full extent of the damage.

definition: A feeling of worry about something, or something that worries you.
example: There is growing public concern about climate change.

definition: To suggest something without saying it directly.
example: Her silence seemed to imply agreement.

definition: Having all its parts; finished.
example: Please ensure your application form is complete before submitting it.

definition: Not finished or not having all the necessary parts.
example: The report was incomplete, lacking important data.

definition: A feeling of great pleasure and satisfaction.
example: To her delight, she passed all her exams.

definition: A number, especially one that is part of an official report or statistic.
example: The latest sales figures show a significant increase.

definition: An organization formed by workers to protect their rights and interests.
example: The workers decided to form a union to negotiate for better conditions.

definition: Not often; seldom.
example: It rarely snows in this part of the country.

definition: To discover something hidden or unknown.
example: The investigation uncovered new evidence in the case.

definition: To place something over or in front of something else to hide or protect it.
example: Please cover the food to keep it fresh.

definition: To follow the movement or progress of someone or something.
example: Scientists are tracking the migration patterns of birds.

definition: A thing that blocks one's way or prevents progress.
example: Lack of funding was a major obstacle to completing the project.

definition: Not right or appropriate for a particular purpose or occasion.
example: His casual clothes were unsuitable for the formal meeting.

definition: To choose a small number of things or people from a larger group.
example: Please select the correct answer from the options provided.

definition: Real, true, or what it is claimed to be; not fake.
example: The museum displays authentic Roman artefacts.

definition: To make something start working or operating.
example: You need to press this button to activate the alarm system.

definition: What is put in, taken in, or operated on by any system or process.
example: We welcome student input on how to improve the course.

definition: To have actual being; to be real.
example: Do you believe life exists on other planets?

definition: An amount of money borrowed from a bank or person that has to be paid back.
example: She took out a loan to buy a new car.

definition: In or to a foreign country, especially across the sea.
example: Many students choose to study overseas for a year.

definition: To get involved in a situation without being asked, especially when your involvement is not wanted or helpful.
example: It's not right to interfere in other people's personal lives.

definition: A feeling of worry, nervousness, or unease about something with an uncertain outcome.
example: Many students experience anxiety before exams.

definition: A particular part or feature of something.
example: We need to consider every aspect of the problem.

definition: Movement or development towards an improved or more advanced state.
example: The project is making good progress towards its completion.

definition: Based on truth or sound reason; acceptable.
example: You need a valid passport to travel internationally.

definition: Only in part; to a limited extent.
example: The road was partially blocked by a fallen tree.

definition: To formally present a document or proposal for consideration or judgment.
example: All students must submit their essays by Friday.

definition: To be made or formed of particular parts or elements.
example: The team consists of five members.

definition: Involving a lot of effort or activity in a short period of time.
example: She took an intensive English course to prepare for her exam.

definition: Worldwide; affecting or involving the whole world.
example: Climate change is a problem that needs to be addressed globally.

definition: The quality of having experience, knowledge, and good judgment.
example: People often seek the wisdom of elders for guidance.

definition: A particular area of knowledge or skill that a person or company is expert in.
example: His speciality is ancient history.

definition: A person who formally requests something, especially a job or a place at a college.
example: There were many qualified applicants for the position.

definition: To express disapproval of or disagreement with something.
example: Many people object to the new building plans.

definition: To surround something completely or include something within something else.
example: Please enclose a copy of your resume with your application.

definition: To state that something is not true, or to refuse to admit or accept something.
example: He denied all the accusations against him.

definition: A building or set of buildings at an airport or station where passengers arrive and depart.
example: Our flight departs from Terminal 2.

definition: To meet someone or experience something, especially unexpectedly.
example: On their trip, they encountered many interesting people.

definition: A formal meeting in a law court where evidence is presented to decide if someone is guilty of a crime.
example: The suspect is currently awaiting trial.
